question: Should durable session persistence and always-on spoken confirmation become the core Talk contract across client-owned and relay voice transports?
rationale: The PR adds a durable SQLite/session model, new gateway RPCs, and a security-sensitive confirmation behavior without a configuration or rollout choice; that product boundary cannot be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Sponsor the core Talk contract
options.body: Approve the durable-session direction, require the compatibility and confirmation fixes plus real behavior proof, then merge through normal review.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Ship only the transcript/session continuity seam and defer spoken confirmation, digest delivery, or cross-client extensions to a separately reviewed follow-up.

options.title: Keep this outside core for now
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers choose a supported voice-session and confirmation product model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core Talk contract
recommendation.body: Approve the durable-session direction, require the compatibility and confirmation fixes plus real behavior proof, then merge through normal review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current assignee and feature proposer is best positioned to present the intended Talk product boundary for maintainer approval.
